                    ### Question
                    A 49-year-old man is diagnosed with hypertension. He has asthma. The creatinine and potassium levels are both slightly elevated. Which of the following anti-hypertensive drugs would be appropriate in his case?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Amlodipine
opb. Propranolol
opc. Enalapril
opd. Hydrochlorothiazide (HCT)
ope. Spironolactone

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In this case, considering the patient's asthma and slightly elevated creatinine and potassium levels, it is advisable to avoid beta-blockers like Propranolol due to potential bronchoconstriction risk and ACE inhibitors like Enalapril due to potential renal and potassium issues. Diuretics like Hydrochlorothiazide (HCT) and potassium-sparing diuretics like Spironolactone should also be avoided. A calcium channel blocker like Amlodipine appears to be a suitable option for this patient with hypertension.
